name: text striping reducer
claim: A lossy striping reducer (stripe-1.0, docs/STRIPE.md) at equal output chars keeps at least 2x the rare (df-1) units and 1.5x the identifier and number units that the head-and-tail `ends` reducer keeps, and lets a cheap model answer what a stored result is about and which identifiers it names with fewer output_read drill-ins; refuted if either ratio falls under 1.2x or the model needs more drill-ins (cf handles ndgwdh, stems gruwry; baseline outstore ends).

models.result: 43 repo blobs, 516 runs, 0 failures. Auto at 0.25 (n >= 2000), stripe over ends: rare 43% vs 27% (1.57x, under the 2x bar, over the 1.2x refutation line), ident 87% vs 33% (2.62x, over 1.5x), num 47% vs 31% (1.49x, just under 1.5x). At 0.1: rare 1.21x, ident 3.18x, num 0.95x. Common (top-decile) units: 38% vs 85% at 0.25, so what ends keeps by position is lost. Lines mode shows no rare gain (0.96x at 0.25). Marker overhead 36%.

Live probe, 36 requests, 6 blobs per condition, one run per cell, no marker legend: fact asks correct full 6/6, stripe 1/6, ends 1/6 (answer present in view: stripe 4/6, ends 1/6); about-sentence keyword score full 0.73, stripe 0.37, ends 0.57 (keywords in view 0.53 vs 0.77). At equal chars the skeleton cost 792 prompt tokens against 532 for ends (fact asks, mean). No benefit shown; n is too small to settle it. Drill-in counts, equal-tokens comparison and silo canary runs not done.

name: striped skeleton notation
claim: The skeleton notation (one header line; kept spans and [~N,wW,lL,kX] markers; `[~` escaped as `[~~`) parses back to the exact source offsets with verify true on 100% of a repo corpus and no collision with markdown or code, at under 30% marker overhead on blobs over 2000 chars; refuted by one failed parse-back or by marker cost above that share (cf ambiguous markers hzzgju; tenet 30, single-line markers).

models.result: Parse-back true on all 43 blobs in all 12 mode and fraction groups (516 runs, 0 failures); determinism by double run, key-order permutation and fingerprint 43/43; idempotent 43/43; header class equals classify() on every reduced row. Overhead part refuted: median marker overhead auto 43% at 0.1, 36% at 0.25, 21% at 0.5; under 30% on only 43 of 126 rows (auto, n >= 2000); chars mode 54% at 0.25. Parse-back holds, the 30% bar does not.

Without a legend the model read the docs skeleton as a corrupted or garbled text and guessed numbers wrong where a value was separated from its label (fact 1/6 on stripe). No legend variant was run, so the cost of the notation to a reader is unmeasured.

name: lexical rarity heuristics
claim: Smoothed document-frequency rarity over whole blob and 25-segment windows, plus structure cues (headings, signal words, identifiers, numbers, keys, line leads), ranks what to keep better than head-and-tail position and than a pure global-rank (Zipf) score, in pure arithmetic with byte-identical output across engines; refuted if rank or IDF-with-logs retains more rare and identifier units at equal chars (docs/STRIPE.md 2.2, open question 16).

models.result: Against head-and-tail only: auto at 0.25 keeps 1.57x the rare units and 2.62x the identifier units of ends at equal chars, and 38% of common units against 85%. Output is identical on double run and on key-order permutation (43/43). The comparison with a rank or IDF-with-logs score was not run, so the second half of the claim is untested. Cost 94 ms per 100 KB (auto, 0.25).

name: reducer class record
claim: A notional class label in the skeleton header (list, headed, json, code, log, tabular, prose, mixed), derived deterministically from line features, picks a cue profile that retains more of the units a reader of that class needs (log lead tokens, json keys) than the class-neutral profile at equal chars; refuted if the class-neutral profile retains as much, or if the label disagrees with the features it was derived from (docs/STRIPE.md 5.1).

models.result: Class profile against class override neutral, same budget, pooled: on log and tabular blobs (9 runs per fraction) lead units kept 90% vs 47% at 0.25 and 39% vs 16% at 0.1, JSON-key units 36% vs 7% and 18% vs 4%, num 40% vs 23% at 0.25; ident at 0.1 lower, 22% vs 41%. On json blobs (10 runs) no difference (keys 6% vs 6%, rare 62% vs 63%). Header label equals classify() on all reduced rows. Label quality issue: see fault on ls-tree. Whether a reader benefits was not measured.

fault: Marker overhead exceeds the 30% provisional bar: median 43% at fraction 0.1, 36% at 0.25, 21% at 0.5 (auto); under 30% on 43 of 126 rows at n >= 2000; chars mode 63% and 54% at 0.1 and 0.25. Markers and header take the output budget the kept spans would use.
handled: Not fixed; recorded only. Output stays within budget (125 of 126 rows within 10%, 0 over). The seams agent decides whether to change the marker form or the bar.

fault: classify() labels tab-separated listings with a single tab per line as prose: tabular needs two or more of | or tab on a line. Repro: 40 lines like '100644 blob a1b2c3d    1000<TAB>app/file0.js' give label prose and all feature shares 0. git ls-tree -r -l output (gen:git-ls-tree, 12000 chars) is labelled prose, so the tabular profile is not used for it.
handled: Not fixed; recorded only (seams fixes). Header class still equals classify() on all rows, so the label is faithful to the rule, not to the data.

fault: chars mode keeps less than auto at equal output chars: rare units 0.41x of ends at 0.1 and 0.96x at 0.25 (auto 1.21x and 1.57x), common units 6% and 16% against 59% and 85%, marker overhead 63% and 54%.
handled: Not fixed; recorded only. Auto is the default; chars mode should not be chosen for log or prose without a reason.

fault: The budget counts chars, but the skeleton costs more tokens per char than head and tail: at equal output chars 792 prompt tokens against 532 for ends (mean, fact asks, 6 blobs), about 49% more. Short kept spans and marker text tokenize poorly.
handled: Not fixed; recorded only. The policy has maxTokens and cpt, but the probe did not compare at equal tokens, so the gap after sizing by tokens is unmeasured.

fault: Given a skeleton with no marker legend, describes it as a corrupted or garbled text (docs blob, about ask) and guesses a number when its label and value were separated by an omission marker (fact asks wrong on 3 of 4 blobs whose answer was in view).
handled: Probe frames were identical across conditions on purpose, so no legend was given and nothing was handled. A frame that explains the markers was not tried.

fault: Injected JavaScript into a source file with a shell heredoc (node - <<EOF); the shell turned the backslash-n escape in a string literal into a real newline and the file failed with a SyntaxError.
handled: Fixed with the Edit tool. Source code that contains backslash escapes goes in through Edit or Write, never through a heredoc or a node string replace.
